items_missed: No agenda statement at all — opened with 'Okay, what was your email address?' and went straight into data collection. Never laid out the roadmap, never gave a 10-15 minute timeframe, never asked 'sound good?'
Never asked 'How are you today?' — no rapport opener whatsoever.

Never offered packing services. Customer said 'we're requesting fifty' boxes, which is a clear packing-adjacent buying signal, and Calvin skipped straight past it. No packing pricing given, no Ecobox referral.

No Worries Damage Coverage named but the $2,000 figure was never stated — customer heard only 'higher evaluation on all your items' and 'well beyond the 60 cents per pound.' The number is what makes the differentiator land.
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops.
Never asked about the garage, patio, or a storage unit — for a two-bedroom apartment described by the customer as 'a three bedroom set up,' the extra-rooms probe was skipped.
Never asked the moving-stressors question ('is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').
No walk-distance question at the origin apartment (unit 210 in an apartment complex) — parking distance to the door is the single biggest hidden time variable on an apartment move.
No sense-check after the clock explanation — rattled off '$208 per hour... fifteen minute increments after two and a half hour minimum' with no 'does that make sense?'

Under-quoted the time and got corrected by the customer: Calvin said 5-7 hours, and Scott pushed back with 'we've done this a couple of times, I think we're closer to seven to eight hours.' The customer had to protect Calvin's own estimate accuracy.
Never asked for the booking. Said 'if you want to move forward with that there's no deposit' but never asked for the yes — no availability close, no 'want to lock that in?'
Never told the customer to reply to the email with corrections, and never explained the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email.
Never gave hours of operation or how to reach the team.
Used the customer's name only twice (once mid-pitch, once at goodbye) — below the 3+ bar.
No 'take a carload' tip, and no 'does that make sense?' to close the prep speech.
top_strength: The clock mechanics and the included-items list were clean and confident: 'Once we get on site there, the hourly rate takes effect... $208 per hour and that includes all the pads and wrap reassembly what the tools will bring... we don't have taxes. We don't have credit card fees,' followed by 'we bill in fifteen minute increments after two and a half hour minimum. So you do just pay for the time that you use that day.' He also handled specialty items proactively and well — volunteering that the 65-inch TV 'will fit in our TV bag,' that the crew can disconnect and reconnect the front-load washer/dryer on pedestals with a liability waiver 'since we aren't certified plumbers,' and that all movers are background checked and trained in-house. When Scott pushed the time estimate up, Calvin adapted fast and gave both numbers ($1,606 at seven hours, $1,814 at eight), which is genuinely useful budget framing.
coaching_note: Calvin, the highest-leverage fix is the missing agenda opener — you cost yourself the whole first section by starting with 'what was your email address?' Open with: 'Thanks for calling, Scott — how are you today? Here's what I'll do: I'll gather some details about your move, then walk you through pricing. Takes about 10-15 minutes. Sound good?' That single 20-second block earns points, sets the customer's expectations, and buys you permission to ask the long probe list without it feeling like an interrogation. Second priority: you left two differentiators and a revenue line on the table. Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee cost you nothing to say and are the two things competitors can't match — add 'a few days before your move we'll email you your mover's photo and info so you know exactly who's showing up, and if we miss the window we agreed on we start discounting your bill immediately.' And when the customer says 'we're requesting fifty' boxes, that is your cue to ask 'are you handling the packing yourself, or would you like a quote on us packing for you?' — you never asked, and on a fifty-box job that's a real second-day sale you walked past. Last thing: you also never asked for the booking. You said there's no deposit, which is the right setup, but then you stopped. Finish it: 'We've got the 14th open — no deposit, and I can move the date free if closing shifts. Want me to lock that in for you now?' You had a customer who was ready, and you handed him a quote instead of a confirmed job.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and competent but transactional — no 'how are you,' no empathy markers, mostly mechanical topic-to-topic transitions, though the 'Yes sir' and 'Thanks Scott, have a great day' kept it friendly and the customer closed warmly with 'thank you so much, appreciate it.'
